solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Escapes (legally!) using gaps in wall

definitions.meaning: ways round a rule that stay within the law
narrow slits in a castle wall for shooting or looking through

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a legal dodge around a rule and a narrow slit in a fortification wall.

clue.text: It goes under short leg, say, for a boundary

indicators.note: in a down clue, the word it is placed below the first piece
short means the word for leg loses its final letter

parts.note: a leg is one example of a limb
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator notes where the short leg fielder stands relative to the boundary rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Short leg is a cricket fielding position near the batter, which makes 'boundary' seem cricket too. 'short' trims LIMB to LIM, and 'goes under' puts IT below it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A limit is a boundary or furthest permitted point, an exact synonym.

clue.text: They rarely row with the opposite sex

definitions.text: They rarely row with the opposite sex

parts.words: They rarely row with the opposite sex
parts.note: sounds like couples who seldom quarrel, but row means pull an oar: women rowers rarely crew with men

explanation.surface: A description of harmonious couples who seldom argue with their partners.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'row' as a quarrel (rhymes with cow) and you picture peaceful couples; read it as rowing a boat (rhymes with go) and you get single-sex crews of women.
explanation.definitionFit: Female rowers usually compete in all-women crews, so they seldom row alongside men.

clue.text: See red, if her tooth should come out

indicators.note: coming out suggests the letters are pulled loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A dental patient fears she will be furious if her tooth has to be extracted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should come out' shuffles the ten letters of IF HER TOOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To see red is to become suddenly furious, the same idiom of losing one's temper.

clue.text: A party's slaves

definitions.meaning: belonging to Labour, a British political party, with the possessive
toils away, works very hard (a verb)

explanation.definitionFit: Labour's is the possessive of the UK party's name, and to labour is to slave away at work.

clue.text: The mysteries of religious teaching in schools

indicators.note: in places the religious teaching inside the word for schools

parts.note: schools of thought, groups sharing a belief, are sects
RE is religious education, a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: A remark on what pupils learn about religion in school, its mysteries included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'schools' is not pupils' schools but schools of thought; RE (religious education) is a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Mysteries are things kept hidden or unknown, which is what confidential matters are.

clue.text: Kind of pollution one gets in respiratory tract

indicators.note: gets in means the numeral for one enters the word for the airway

parts.note: the nose is the start of the respiratory tract
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A health warning that some airborne pollution enters your breathing passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive sound is classed as noise pollution, a recognised environmental nuisance.

clue.text: Four points given for intelligence

parts.note: N for north, one of the four compass points
E for east
W for west
S for south

explanation.surface: A scoring note: four points are awarded for showing intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of information received, as in military intelligence, is news.

clue.text: Anger conceals extremes of emotion for her

indicators.note: conceals means the word for anger holds something hidden inside it

parts.note: ire is an old word for anger

indicators.note: extremes are the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone's rage masks the strong feelings she has for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' is the whole definition: the answer is simply a woman's name, which the surface hides by making 'her' look like the object of feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so the pronoun stands in for a female person.

clue.text: They blow up king and generals in a revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Rebels blow up the king and his generals during an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a revolution' rearranges R (king) with GENERALS. 'Blow up' sounds like explosives but means enlarging photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Photographic enlargers project negatives to make larger prints, that is, blow them up.

clue.text: Scholar, turncoat and murdered radical

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate scholar
a rat is someone who deserts his side

explanation.surface: A list of three figures: an academic, a traitor and an assassinated revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Marat, French Revolution radical journalist, was stabbed in his bath by Charlotte Corday.

clue.text: A farthing on Victorian transport?

parts.note: the penny-farthing bicycle had a big front wheel (penny) and a small rear one (farthing)

explanation.surface: A question about what a tiny coin was worth on a nineteenth-century carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny. On a penny-farthing bicycle the small rear wheel was the farthing.
explanation.definitionFit: On the penny-farthing bicycle, the small wheel at the rear is the part called the farthing.

clue.text: MPs' second homes, perhaps

parts.note: members of Parliament from the regions often keep a residence in the city as well as their constituency home

explanation.surface: A dig at the second homes MPs claim expenses for.
explanation.walkthrough: MPs who live in their constituency often keep a second home in London; 'Houses' also hints at the Houses of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A city residence kept by someone whose main home is in the country is a classic London second home.

clue.text: Lord Peter sacrificed what, ultimately?

indicators.note: sacrificed means the name gives up a letter
ultimately points to the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A question about what an aristocrat called Peter gave up in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' picks T, the last letter of what, and 'sacrificed' removes it from PETER.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, such as a lord in the House of Lords.

clue.text: Book depressing accommodation

parts.note: bleak means grim or depressing
a house is a dwelling, somewhere to live

explanation.surface: Someone books a room and finds it dismal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve, matching 'accommodation', but it is the definition: a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak House is a novel by Charles Dickens, so it is a book by title.

clue.text: Misread, tragically, what a lover does

indicators.note: things going tragically wrong suggests the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A lover's message tragically misunderstood, as in a romantic tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tragically' rearranges the letters of MISREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in love looks upon the beloved with warm approval and regard.

clue.text: The PM for a No Ten revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Talk of a Prime Minister plotting an uprising at Number Ten Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister, whose home is No 10 Downing Street, but it means post meridiem. 'revolution' rearranges FOR A NO TEN.
explanation.definitionFit: PM, post meridiem, labels the hours after midday, the period between noon and evening.

clue.text: Old sailor, one about to get cross

parts.note: an old salt is a veteran sailor
I is the Roman numeral one
re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: A veteran seaman is on the point of losing his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like angry but is a noun: the X-shaped cross of St Andrew on the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross in heraldry, as on Scotland's flag.

clue.text: Whisky, for example, from NE Britain

indicators.note: from signals that the answer is made out of the letters that follow

explanation.surface: Whisky as a famous product of north-east Britain, that is Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' here means made from: rearrange the letters of NE BRITAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An intoxicating drink is an inebriant, and whisky is one example.

clue.text: Rolled metal, useless for fencing

definitions.meaning: thin metal sheet rolled out for kitchen use
a fencing sword made of flimsy kitchen metal would be no use at all

explanation.definitionFit: Kitchen wrapping is thin rolled sheet metal, and a sword of that stuff would bend uselessly.

clue.text: Like a cat pedigree, including one variety

indicators.note: including means the word for pedigree takes something inside it

parts.note: a pedigree is a line of descent

indicators.note: a variety is a different form, so the letters of one are rearranged

explanation.surface: A show cat's pedigree, with one breed variety listed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like a cat' reads as describing the pedigree animal, but it is the definition: lion-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonine means lion-like, and the lion is the great member of the cat family.

clue.text: Fire risks in evidence at Henley regatta?

definitions.meaning: things that blaze, a fire hazard
coloured club jackets worn at the Henley rowing regatta

explanation.walkthrough: Henley Royal Regatta is a rowing event on the Thames, famous for spectators in striped club jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that blaze are fire risks, and colourful club jackets are traditional dress at Henley.

clue.text: Mind what you do when parents are out

definitions.meaning: look after, take care of a child

definitions.text: what you do when parents are out
definitions.meaning: the job of watching children while the parents are away

explanation.definitionFit: To mind children is to look after them, which is the job done while parents go out.

clue.text: Bird that was once British

definitions.meaning: a marsh bird such as the water ...
British ... was the old nationalised railway of Britain

explanation.definitionFit: The rail is a wading bird, and British Rail was the former state railway operator.

clue.text: Popular support up country

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: aid means help or support

explanation.surface: Popular support rises across the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses AID to DIA in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a nation in South Asia, so it is a country.

clue.text: A morris-dancer's obsession

parts.note: a fixation, and also the prop of a horse's head on a stick carried in morris dancing

explanation.surface: A folk dancer's fixation with dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Morris dancing is English folk dancing, often with a performer carrying a mock horse. The clue also means a pet obsession.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet subject someone constantly returns to, and also a mock horse carried in folk dances.

clue.text: Englishmen take note, get rid of faults

parts.note: E is short for English
men, the second part of the word
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Englishmen are told to take heed and correct their faults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Englishmen' splits into E (English) and MEN; 'take' only joins the note on.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text by removing its errors.

clue.text: A goddess of Erin? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls short by its final letter

parts.note: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland, so of Erin means Irish

explanation.surface: A question whether a goddess was Irish, not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' cuts the last letter from IRISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is the Greek goddess of the rainbow and a messenger of the gods.

clue.text: Junior soldiers in command — don't believe them!

parts.note: an order is a command
lies are untruths, not to be believed

explanation.surface: A warning not to trust junior soldiers placed in command.
explanation.definitionFit: Orderlies are soldiers assigned to attend officers or carry out menial duties.

clue.text: University guru finds employment

parts.note: a sage is a wise teacher, a guru

explanation.surface: A university's wise man lands a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means use or employment, as in the employment of a word or tool.

clue.text: Lone arsonist gets closer inside

indicators.note: inside means the answer sits within the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: A solitary arsonist creeps nearer to the building.
explanation.definitionFit: To near is to approach or draw closer, a direct synonym of the verb phrase.

clue.text: Nurse, in dire need, organised petition

indicators.note: in places the word for nurse within the rearranged letters
dire suggests something in a bad way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: to nurse a patient is to treat them

explanation.surface: A nurse, badly in need, got up a petition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' rearranges NEED to EN..ED around TREAT. 'organised petition' stands for a past-tense verb: petitioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or plead, so having made an earnest plea fits the definition.
